title: The ethical ambiguity of Al data enrichment: Measuring gaps in research ethics norms and practices
benchmark_measurement: The paper did not measure any aspect of faith or religion. The study is a meta-analysis measuring the gaps in research ethics norms and practices (e.g., disclosure of IRB review, payment, consent, demographics) in AI research papers that use crowdsourcing for data enrichment.
findings: The paper does not contain any findings related to religion. The key findings are that leading AI research venues (like ICLR and NeurIPS) have emerging but inconsistently followed ethics policies for research involving crowdsourced human workers. Compared to fields like Psychology, AI research papers are significantly less likely to disclose ethics reviews, payment details, and worker demographics, even when conducting similar types of behavioral studies.
